correctness.rationale: KKT radial reduction yields one monotone scalar root, whose smooth active-chart Jacobians were independently reconstructed and checked by finite differences. Convexity in the radius ratio and Cauchy--Schwarz reduce every row to two sharp branches; extremizing smooth charts establish both lower bounds. Strict concavity proves the unique inner maximizer and an expansion proves the crossover asymptotic. The open zero-radius and unchanged-vector regions have maximum-norm derivatives at most one; generic translated segment integration handles switching boundaries and yields the global Lipschitz bound. 164490 finite assertions replayed, supplementary not proof.

value.rationale: The result exactly solves a natural coordinatewise stability problem for the established extended Lorentz cones across all finite dimensions. It reveals that nonexpansivity holds only in the polyhedral radial dimension one, and it characterizes a genuine scalar-output/vector-output sensitivity phase boundary with sqrt(vector dimension) scaling. This quantitative classification of a nonlinear metric projector is not a textbook one-step consequence of Euclidean nonexpansivity.
